newsitem.title: INDIA: Four Asian nations to form huge new economic forum.
newsitem.headline: Four Asian nations to form huge new economic forum.

text.p: Four Asian neighbours will launch an economic grouping next week which will encircle 10 percent of the global market and cover one billion people, Indian and Thai officials said on Thursday.
Government ministers will launch the Bangladesh India Sri Lanka Thailand Economic Cooperation (BISTEC) forum at a meeting on June 6 at Bangkok, they said.

India, Pakistan, Sri Lanka, Bangladesh, Bhutan, Nepal and the Maldives form the seven-nation South Asian Association of of Regional Cooperation (SAARC), whose members will form a South Asian Free Trade Area by 2001.

The Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN) -- grouping Brunei, Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesia, the Philippines, Singapore and Vietnam -- is already a high-growth economic zone the South Asian nations seek to emulate.

"It (BISTEC) is in the line of growth triangles or quadrangles," said a senior Indian Foreign Ministry official, who asked not to be named. "Right now we are not talking about a trading bloc as such."
"It is not yet a preferential trade arrangment but there are very strong intentions on investment promotion and joint ventures to harness synergies," the official said.
While the group was scheduled to be launched on June 6, detailed studies on economic cooperation would take a year, and institutional arrangements would follow later, the Indian official said.

All four nations lie along the rim of the Bay of Bengal. Together, they comprise one billion people and 10 percent of the world market, Thai deputy foreign minister Pitak Intravitayanunt said before addressing a business meeting in the Indian capital.

India's human resources, technical expertise, market size, and its membership of the SAARC and the Indian Ocean Rim Association for Regional Cooperation offered "tremendous potential" for BISTEC, the Thai leader said.
